security_audit.summary: The skill is not malicious, but it depends on broad belt CLI access and third-party inference services. Real command and network findings were confirmed, while markdown diagrams, templates, and the line 207 reconnaissance hit were dismissed as false positives. Publication should require clear user confirmation for login, installs, remote app runs, and possible service costs.

remediation.suggestion: Narrow allowed tools to required belt subcommands, or require explicit confirmation before login, app listing, and remote job execution.
Tell users before execution that prompts, image references, and LoRA paths may be sent to inference.sh or model providers.
Keep npx skill-install commands as optional manual steps, and avoid asking agents to execute them automatically.

content.value_statement: AI image generators often change a character between images. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through reference sheets, description anchors, and LoRA planning.
actual_capabilities: Explains turnaround, expression, outfit, and color palette sheet formats.
Provides prompt patterns for FLUX and LoRA character generation.
Defines a reusable description-anchor method for consistent prompts.
Recommends LoRA trigger words, reference image counts, and scale ranges.
Lists common consistency failures with practical mitigations.
limitations: Command examples require the belt CLI and an inference.sh login.
The skill does not train a LoRA by itself.
Exact visual consistency still depends on model behavior and reference quality.
Remote generation may send prompt data to third-party services.

use_cases.title: Prepare Game Character References
use_cases.description: Build front, side, back, outfit, and color references before producing game art.

use_cases.title: Plan Comic Expression Sheets
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable face and emotion set for recurring comic or visual novel characters.

use_cases.title: Standardize AI Art Direction
use_cases.description: Document anchors, palettes, and LoRA notes so a team can generate consistent scenes.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Character Sheet
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new character.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a character design sheet plan for [character idea]. Include a description anchor, turnaround views, expressions, palette notes, and missing questions.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Turnaround Prompt Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this character description into matching front, three-quarter, side, and back view prompts. Keep the identity details unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Consistency Drift
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my character prompts for consistency drift. Identify weak visual anchors, missing color details, and changes that may alter the character.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a LoRA Character Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for many generated images.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a LoRA preparation plan for this character. Specify reference image coverage, trigger wording, scale guidance, sheet outputs, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: I need a recurring fantasy merchant for a game prototype.
output: A reusable 50-word visual anchor for the merchant.
A four-view turnaround plan with fixed clothing and proportions.
A palette record for skin, hair, fabric, trim, and accessories.

output_examples.input: My comic character changes face shape between images.
output: A drift diagnosis focused on vague age, hair, eye, and face cues.
A stronger prompt structure that repeats identity details first.
An expression sheet plan for neutral, happy, angry, sad, surprised, and thinking views.

output_examples.input: I want to use a LoRA for a long visual novel project.
output: A reference image coverage checklist for poses, lighting, outfits, and close-ups.
A trigger word and scale recommendation for consistent character recall.
A validation plan comparing generated scenes against the reference sheet.

best_practices: Write a detailed description anchor and reuse it exactly.
Record exact colors, proportions, clothing, and distinguishing marks.
Generate reference views and expressions before complex scene images.
anti_patterns: Starting scene generation before defining a reference sheet.
Using vague traits such as young, cool outfit, or red hair.
Changing identity details or prompt order between generations.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images directly?
faq.answer: It provides guidance and command examples. Direct generation requires the belt CLI and a compatible inference service.

faq.question: Can it guarantee identical characters?
faq.answer: No. It improves consistency through anchors, sheets, and LoRA planning, but model output can still vary.

faq.question: What is a description anchor?
faq.answer: It is a detailed identity paragraph reused in every prompt so the model sees stable character details.

faq.question: When should I use LoRA?
faq.answer: Use LoRA when a project needs many images of the same character across scenes, poses, or outfits.

faq.question: Is this useful without the belt CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The reference sheet methods and prompt structure can be used with other image generation tools.

faq.question: What data may leave my machine?
faq.answer: Prompt text, image references, and LoRA paths may be sent when you run remote inference commands.
